Regarding the physical therapy techniques for lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow), the described plan is highly effective and aligns with current clinical best practices. Lateral epicondylitis is primarily a tendinopathy involving the extensor carpi radialis brevis tendon. The prescription of eccentric strengthening exercises is considered the gold standard in rehabilitation for this condition, as it promotes collagen realignment and improves tendon load tolerance. Manual therapy can help address associated soft tissue restrictions and improve joint mobility, while ice therapy serves as an appropriate adjunct for managing acute pain and inflammation post-exercise. This multimodal approach addresses both the mechanical dysfunction and the symptomatic pain, facilitating a return to activity.
